name: Brand Anthem Montage
definition: Cinematic anthem montage of a pro sports team/event the brand now sponsors (crowd, stadium with logo, players drinking product, goals), closes on co-branded lockup; announces the partnership rather than selling the product.
closest: Win (Victory Announcement) - both announce a milestone, but this is a produced brand-film montage borrowing a team's fandom, not raw social proof

name: Partner Glow-Up (She Fixed Him)
definition: The buyer is the partner: girlfriend/wife on camera says men are clueless, shows how she 'built' her man with the product (applying it to him), ends on the visible result + couple affection and a CTA aimed at partners to buy for him.
closest: Personal Story / Lesson From Others - but the narrator is the partner who buys and applies the product to someone else, targeting the gift/partner purchaser

name: Motion-Graphic Packshot
definition: No people: flat brand-color frames with kinetic headline type ('NEW!', '12g protein / 0g sugar') while packshots animate in, ending on per-variant 'Shop Now' cards. A moving catalog/launch card.
closest: Product Demo Ads - but nothing is used or demonstrated; it is an animated static/spec card

name: Video Static (Headline Over Looping B-roll)
definition: Whole ad = one short lo-fi product b-roll loop (pour/stir the drink) with a single meme/headline caption burned on top and a product tag; no talking, no story, reads like an organic story post or a moving static image ad.
closest: Satisfying B-roll (Front-Splice) - that is a hook spliced in front of another ad; here the b-roll + one caption IS the entire ad. Text-Wall Story uses a still and a long story

name: Timestamped Real-Time Test
definition: Creator takes the product on camera and logs its effect live with big on-screen clock timestamps (8:40pm mix, 9:08pm 'jaw loosening', 9:43pm asleep); the clock jumps carry the proof in one sitting.
closest: Challenge ('I tried X for 7 days') - same proof logic but compressed into minutes/hours of one session with timestamp cuts instead of days

name: Offer Stack Breakdown
definition: Whole ad is the deal: provocative offer hook ('Don't buy X until you hear this', 'We need to apologize to anyone who bought before this deal'), then VO/captions walk item-by-item through what's in the bundle + free gifts + % off over fast lifestyle/b-roll clips, persistent discount banner, scarcity close ('grab yours before it's too late').
closest: Unboxing / Product Demo - but the subject is the offer (bundle contents, gifts, price) not the product experience; it's an infomercial-style value stack

name: IP Collab Drop Trailer
definition: Movie-trailer-style launch of a limited-edition product co-branded with a film/TV franchise: dramatic set dressing in the show's world, VFX (lasers, explosions), hero packshots, product in use, franchise logo + URL end card. The borrowed IP is the hook.
closest: Reaction / Trend-Hijack (Borrowed Fame) - borrows existing attention, but via an official licensed product drop styled as a trailer, not a reaction clip

name: Celebrity Cameo Commercial
definition: Short, polished TV-style spot built entirely around a famous celebrity using the product on a styled set, with bold kinetic claim supers ('Natural spray', '72 hour protection') and a retail end card. Fame is the hook; no testimony or story.
closest: Celebrity Podcast Clip / TV Segment Clip - those borrow existing footage; here the brand hires the celebrity for an original commercial

name: Absurdist Brand Vignette
definition: One surreal, staged visual gag (a bubble bath in a pickup bed in the woods) shot cinematically, 6-10s, one caption at most ('Lost in the suds'), product barely shown; pure brand-world absurdity meant to stop the scroll.
closest: Scenarios - opens on a hypothetical but explains it; this is a wordless visual joke with no pitch

name: Retail Aisle Find
definition: Shopper-POV video shot inside a big-box retailer: walks to the display, holds up the pack against the shelf, calls out the price/value, drops it in the cart, quick at-home use, CTA to grab it on your next store run. Sells availability + deal at a specific retailer.
closest: Day In The Life / UGC Reviews - but the store shelf, price tag and 'next haul' CTA are the structure; it drives retail, not DTC

name: Split-Self Skit (Creator Plays Both Roles)
definition: One creator plays two characters cut back and forth (different shirts/props): the 'problem' self with bad habits voices symptoms and objections, the 'expert' self diagnoses and pitches the product, ending with the convert won over + CTA.
closest: Problem-Agitate-Solve / Myth Buster - same beats but delivered as a scripted two-character dialogue skit by one person

name: 3D Render Feature Tour
definition: All-CGI hero render of the product rotating through close-ups with engineering callouts (angles, arrows, materials, exploded view) one feature per beat, ending on a tagline. Sells precision/build quality without any human.
closest: Animated Mechanism Explainer - that animates the body/biology; this animates the product's engineering

name: Week-of-Meals Cost Tally
definition: Day-by-day sequence (Mon to Fri) preparing one serving per day, each with a cumulative running-cost sticker that ticks up, ending under a headline price cap ('a week for <$15'). The math reveal is the hook.
closest: Levels / UGC Listicle - sequential beats, but structured as a calendar week with a running price total proving value

name: Recipe Reel (Product as Ingredient)
definition: Food-creator recipe video where the product is an ingredient in something craveable (bars, s'mores, pancakes): hero bite first, then hands-only mixing steps, ingredient/directions card, final bite + CTA. Sells taste and versatility rather than the product's own claims.
closest: UGC How-To - that shows how to use the product as intended; here the product disappears into a new recipe and the recipe is the content
